Folks — technical notes and proposed verification steps (executive summary first):

Summary: On receipt at the depot gate the operator should perform a deterministic hash verification (SHA-256) against our signed manifest, run the origin-scan (we will supply a compact scanner binary and an allowlist), and then verify the signing chain. If checks pass, the operator will perform the two-person acceptance (operator + depot rep) and record their fingerprints in the custody manifest.

Detailed steps (to include in the one-page checklist):
- Step 0: Prior to dispatch, we will sign the manifest with our signing key (fingerprint: RWI-AB12-CD34).
- Step 1: At handoff, compute SHA-256 for each artifact and compare to manifest.
- Step 2: Run origin-scan with flags: --tight-allowlist --no-network --report-json origin-scan-report.json. Scanner will run in isolated environment on courier laptop.
- Step 3: Verify embedded third-party signatures (if any) and note any unknown provenance.
- Step 4: Operator key ceremony: exchange operator timestamps and one-time nonce; record on manifest.
- Step 5: If any high-severity provenance flags, quarantine bundle and escalate to Karthik (karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com).

I attached a lightweight verification script and an example origin-scan output. We are also including a compact checksum verifier (no network calls).

Attachments: [rwi-verifier-1.0.sh] (text/x-sh), [origin-scan-example.json] (application/json)

I will produce the official origin-scan report after simulating the scanner against the sealed bundle we have in staging. Expect report and signed-manifest by EOD.

- Priyom
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
